meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. I have twenty minutes, so tell me who decided that and on what basis.
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.

My son doesn't cheat, and he doesn't lie to me. You say you can prove it, so put it on the table, because right now all I've heard is an accusation and a zero that went in before anyone picked up a phone. I'm writing down that you said "your son cheated."
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.

I'm not explaining anything, Hale; I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Turn the screen and show me that history, whose account it's under and what date it's on, because I read documents myself. And pasting text into a file tells you where it was pasted from, not who wrote it, so was Owen asked about this before you entered the zero?
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.

Read me the line exactly as it appears in Owen's essay, Hale, and I'll check Act 3, Scene 2 myself tonight. A misquote is something a tired seventeen-year-old does, not a confession. You've now given me two things and still haven't shown me a single page, so turn the screen.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.

"He lied to you." My son doesn't lie, Hale, and you've just told his mother she can't tell when her own child is lying, so are you calling me a fool or a liar? You've had two minutes to turn that screen and you've spent them on accusations instead, so either show me the documents or I'm walking upstairs to the principal's office when we're done here.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

"Take it or leave it." Your own procedure, 4.2, says you contact me before any mark is entered, and you didn't, so that zero was never properly there and I'm not bargaining it back from you. Before I take anything, I want to know who decided this, and whether anything about it is sitting on Owen's record right now.
Well, nothing; I asked you two questions and you've answered neither. Who decided, and is it on his file, yes or no. I'm waiting, Hale.
